translations.answer: The maintainer explains that the quality matrix maps acceleration in the space of the configuration to force in the cotangent space. The FreeFlyer motion and force components are both represented in the first rigid body coordinate system. The author first verifies that the fixed base matrix is completely consistent and that the FK poses are consistent on both sides, then clears the floating base position and sets the pose to the unit. At this point, the matrix error is reduced to about 1e-8 to 1e-10. The experiment supports that the reference system representation is the main difference, but no thread provides a complete matrix transformation formula for any pose.
translations.applicability: This applies to the original post FreeFlyer model's CRBA/MuJoCo full mass matrix comparison; it cannot be used directly to replace the generalized coordinate base transformation of the target project.
translations.credibility.rationale: There is engineering record on environment, processing steps and results, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: The maintainer provides data.oMi[1].rotation.T * Jc comparison; the author applies rotation and reports the error significantly decreases.
translations.details.attempts.1: The author compares fixed base and FreeFlyer, and sets both base poses to unit; at unit pose, the matrix error is reduced to about 1e-8 to 1e-10.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: First determine the coordinate system and point of action of the Jacobian to be compared; rotate Pinocchio world frame Jcom to the target local coordinate system and then compare.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Compare using unit base rotation and non-unit rotation of CRBA, to confirm if the difference is only due to the floating base representation.
translations.details.diagnostics.2: Use RNEA and a suitable reference system to cross-validate the quality matrix, rather than comparing element-wise between two libraries' original matrices.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Compare Jcom before converting both sides to the same coordinate expression; the original thread used data.oMi[1].rotation.T * Pinocchio Jc for the first floating rigid body.
translations.details.effective_fixes.1: When reading joint local velocities, first perform forward kinematics (model, data, q, qdot), then use data.v[id]; only change the coordinate expression by rotating linear and angular components, not translating the point of action.
translations.details.environments.0: 2018 Pinocchio Python/C++, MuJoCo comparison; user provides minimal URDF, two-legged URDF state and full matrix output; specific release version not mentioned.
translations.details.limits.0: The original thread did not provide a general MuJoCo↔Pinocchio base transformation formula, and did not fully close all bias term differences.
translations.details.limits.1: data.oMi[1] is only suitable for the minimal model's first target joint; actual systems must use correct joint ID.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The author confirms that the Jcom rotation difference from MuJoCo is significantly reduced and that WORLD/LOCAL explanation is clear.
translations.details.outcomes.1: The author obtains nearly consistent mass matrices on both sides of Jcom during unit base rotation experiment, and attributes the remaining non-unit rotation difference to the floating base representation.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why are the first three columns of Jcom in the floating base not the identity matrix, and are the values of the Pinocchio and MuJoCo mass matrices different?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: What is the correspondence between Pinocchio's WORLD, LOCAL Jacobian, and data.v[id] in terms of point of action and coordinate system?
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Pinocchio's Jcom is expressed in world coordinates; the user's MuJoCo comparison is interpreted as a waist local coordinate system.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: Pinocchio's floating base velocity, acceleration, and force components are expressed in first rigid body coordinates, while the MuJoCo comparison matrix is expressed in world coordinates.
translations.details.symptoms.0: When the floating base is not unit, the first three columns of Pinocchio's Jcom show a non-diagonal element of about 1e-2, while the user expects an identity matrix.
translations.details.symptoms.1: The fixed base mass matrix is consistent on both sides, but becomes significantly different after adding FreeFlyer and rotating the base to non-unit pose.
translations.source.locator: Issue #446, maintainer's mass matrix representation explanation in issuecomment-380809974; author's unit pose comparison in issuecomment-381078728
translations.source.title: Pinocchio and MuJoCo's Floating Base Jcom and Inertial Matrix Differences Need to Be Aligned on Reference System Representation
